newsitem.title: USA: Mass. governor, Boston mayor seek tax exemptions.
newsitem.headline: Mass. governor, Boston mayor seek tax exemptions.

text.p: Massachusetts Governor William Weld, who is waiting to be confirmed as the next U.S. ambassador to Mexico, pushed one more time for another state tax cut on Tuesday.
Weld, testifying before the joint Taxation Committee, supported a proposal to exempt Internet services and software developers from the state's 5 percent telecommunications sales tax.

The governor said the state's Internet industry will continue to expand rapidly and create new jobs, "that is if we don't blow it and stifle that growth. We think that's exactly what the 5 percent tax does."
"The repeal of internet taxes in competitive states like New York and California really should set off alarm clocks here," Weld added.

Rep. Daniel Bosley (D-North Adams), who filed the internet tax bill, followed Weld, who had been met with the now-inevitable choruses of "Buenos dias, governor," when he launched his own testimony. "Now that he's leaving, I'm starting to agree with him on stuff," Bosley joked, alluding to Weld's expected nomination.
Weld and the state Legislature have enacted 11 tax cuts in the past six years.

As Weld supported sales tax exemptions for sections of an industry, Boston Mayor Thomas Menino said he wanted the same thing for sections of the state - low-income neighborhoods, and communities threatened by sales-tax-free New Hampshire.

Menino testified in favor of creating "sales-tax-free zones" in parts of Boston and the Merrimack Valley, in order to attract new businesses. The proposal would require developers to create a certain number of new jobs before becoming eligible for the tax exemption.

"These are good economic times, but that doesn't mean we can rest on our laurels," Menino said, pointing to a high level of poverty in the Merrimack Valley, where jobs are often lost to the Granite State.
